situation:
You are the operations manager at HOLLOWAY PRESS, a commercial print shop that has served regional retailers for thirty years. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend how the shop should answer a new competitor, and to present that recommendation this afternoon.

HOLLOWAY PRESS prints shelf signage and in-store displays, and its operators know each retailer's account by memory, which store changes its window monthly and which one buys on price. BRIGHTFOLD, a two-year-old competitor, quotes online in minutes and has taken four accounts this year.

The shop could buy the same automated workflow. It would match BRIGHTFOLD on turnaround, but the operators have resisted it for two years and several would leave rather than learn it, taking the account knowledge with them. BRIGHTFOLD has instead offered to route overflow printing to Holloway at a guaranteed volume, under its own name and pricing.

That revenue is steady and costs the shop nothing to start. The retailers who order through it would become BRIGHTFOLD's customers rather than the shop's, and the operators would keep the work without keeping the accounts. The owner (judge) wants your recommendation and the reasoning behind it.

You will present it to the owner (judge) in the owner's office. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
